gaps.lead: It's a pity you didn't tell me earlier.
gaps.explanation: should/ought to have + participle expresses past regret/advice.

gaps.lead: Her French improved because she lived in Lyon.
gaps.sentence: Her French improved as ___ in Lyon.
gaps.explanation: as a result of + noun/-ing: as a result of living.

gaps.lead: She started working here five years ago.
gaps.explanation: Action starting in the past and continuing: has been working (present perfect continuous).

gaps.lead: 'Have you seen my keys anywhere?' he asked us.
gaps.sentence: He asked us ___ seen his keys anywhere.
gaps.explanation: if/whether + subject + had + participle: whether we had seen.

gaps.lead: I can't wait for the holidays to begin.
gaps.explanation: look forward TO + -ing/noun: looking forward to the holidays beginning.

gaps.lead: People say the castle is haunted.
gaps.explanation: People say → It is said… / The castle is said to be…
